evals.prompt: How do I add Medusa heads to Vicuna-7B and train them?
evals.expected_output: Explains Medusa: adding several extra decoding heads to the base model, training them (Medusa-1 with frozen backbone, optionally Medusa-2 with joint fine-tuning), and using tree-based attention for verification. Mentions the FasterDecoding/Medusa repo and that Medusa-1 is lossless.

evals.prompt: I'm running Llama-2-70B on 4xA100 for a code-completion tool, and p50 latency per token is about 45ms, which is too slow for our IDE plugin. I have Llama-2-7B and TinyLlama-1.1B checkpoints available. In HF transformers, how can I use one of them to speed up generation without changing the 70B outputs? Please include the assistant_model setup and how to choose the number of speculative tokens.
evals.expected_output: Recommends draft-model speculative decoding with a small draft model sharing the 70B tokenizer. Gives a working assistant_model example and tuning guidance for the number of draft tokens (K) based on acceptance rate. Notes a draft that is 5-10x smaller is best, so the 7B is the more suitable choice, and that the output distribution matches the target model.

evals.prompt: We can't afford to train anything or host a second model. Is there a way to get our existing LLM to produce several tokens per forward pass by solving the decoding as a parallel fixed-point problem? Which settings matter?
evals.expected_output: Identifies Lookahead Decoding, which uses Jacobi iteration with n-gram collection and verification and needs no draft model or training. Explains the window size W and n-gram size N parameters, and the typical speedup of about 1.5-2.3x, higher for code.

evals.prompt: I need to serve Llama-3-8B behind an OpenAI-compatible API with continuous batching and AWQ quantization on a single 24GB GPU. How do I set that up?
evals.expected_output: Recommends vLLM with PagedAttention, continuous batching, AWQ quantization flags and the OpenAI-compatible server. It does not center on speculative decoding.

evals.prompt: Set up Phoenix tracing for my LLM app so I can see latency per span and run evaluations on a dataset of production traces.
evals.expected_output: Explains how to instrument the app with Phoenix/OpenTelemetry tracing, inspect span latencies and run dataset evaluations. It does not cover inference acceleration techniques.
